## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates real-world CNF governance under multi-region and partition scenarios, focusing on provenance, attestation, and policy enforcement using Sigstore, SBOM, Kyverno/OPA, and distributed consistency.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore/cosign SBOM provenance
- Quorum-based replication and central verifier
- Kyverno/OPA regional policy gates
- TPM/IMA attestation mechanisms
- Partition-tolerant rollout strategies
- In-namespace test scaffolding for rollback safety

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-attestation-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attestation-sbom-check
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Deployment upgrade requires attestationDigest and sbomDigest"
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations.attestationDigest: "*"
        metadata.annotations.sbomDigest: "*"
```

- How would you model failure modes during partition events and ensure eventual consistency?
- What metrics and dashboards would you expose to detect drift between regional verifiers and the central ledger?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This question assesses your understanding of certificate rotation, CSR workflows, SPIFFE identities, and tenant isolation in Kubernetes-based CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway platforms. It validates your ability to design lifecycle management solutions that operate without downtime and your competence in developing testable configurations before production rollout.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant CSR issuance within Kubernetes
- Rotating CA with short-lived certificates for enhanced security
- SPIFFE identities and TLS handshakes in multi-tenant CNF gateways
- Tenant isolation using separate namespaces

## Solution Architecture

### 1. Minimal CA Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca
  namespace: cnf-gateway
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  ca.crt: <base64-encoded-CA-certificate>
  ca.key: <base64-encoded-CA-private-key>
```

### 2. CSR Flow and Approval Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-csr
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  groups:
  - system:authenticated
  request: <base64-encoded-CSR>
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
---
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-csr
spec:
  approval:
  - user: system:controller:certificates-approver
    approval: true
  conditions:
  - type: Approved
    reason: TenantIdentityValidated
    message: CSR identity matches tenant namespace
```

### 3. Per-Tenant CA Rotation Policy (30-Day Renewal)

```yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: gateway-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: gateway-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  commonName: gateway.tenant-a.cnf
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.cnf
  spiffeURIs:
  - spiffe://cnf/tenant-a/gateway
  duration: 720h # 30 days
  renewBefore: 168h # 7 days before expiry
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
  - server auth
```

### 4. Test Manifest with Sidecar Validation

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant-id: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8443
    targetPort: 8443
  selector:
    app: gateway
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
        env:
        - name: SPIFFE_ID
          value: spiffe://cnf/tenant-a/gateway
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: gateway-tls
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-validator
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: validator
    image: curl:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c"]
    args:
    - |
      # Validate TLS handshake
      openssl s_client -connect gateway:8443 \
        -CAfile /etc/tls/ca.crt \
        -cert /etc/tls/tls.crt \
        -key /etc/tls/tls.key \
        -verify_return_error
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls-certs
      mountPath: /etc/tls
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: tls-certs
    secret:
      secretName: gateway-tls
```

### 5. SPIFFE Identity Validation

Each tenant receives a SPIFFE identity in the format `spiffe://cnf/{tenant}/gateway`. The CSR approval policy validates that the requested identity matches the tenant's namespace before issuance, ensuring strict tenant isolation.

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical disaster recovery design for CNF gateways with multi-tenancy, moving beyond high-level theory to real implementation.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes CRD design for per-tenant failover policies
- Control-plane health probes with configurable thresholds
- Traffic re-routing via Ingress/VirtualService resources
- TLS identity preservation using SPIFFE/SPIRE

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFailoverPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-failover
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  primaryGateway: gateway-a.tenant-a.svc
  standbyGateway: gateway-a-standby.tenant-a.svc
  unhealthyThreshold: 3
  failoverDelaySeconds: 5
  tlsIdentityRef:
    spireEntry: spiffe://cluster/tenant-a/gateway
```

```go
// Controller reconciliation logic (simplified)
func (r *TenantFailoverPolicyReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) error {
    policy := &cnfv1.TenantFailoverPolicy{}
    if err := r.Get(ctx, req.NamespacedName, policy); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    // Poll control-plane health
    healthy := r.checkControlPlaneHealth(policy.Spec.Tenant)

    if !healthy {
        policy.Status.FailureCount++
        if policy.Status.FailureCount >= policy.Spec.UnhealthyThreshold {
            return r.executeFailover(policy)
        }
    } else {
        policy.Status.FailureCount = 0
    }
    return nil
}

func (r *TenantFailoverPolicyReconciler) executeFailover(policy *cnfv1.TenantFailoverPolicy) error {
    // Update Ingress to point to standby
    ingress := &networkingv1.Ingress{}
    r.Get(ctx, types.NamespacedName{Name: "gateway-ingress", Namespace: policy.Spec.Tenant}, ingress)
    ingress.Spec.Default.Backend.Service.Name = policy.Spec.StandbyGateway
    r.Update(ctx, ingress)

    // Update SPIRE TLS identity binding
    return r.updateSPIREEntry(policy)
}
```

Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical policy design and enforcement in a real multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on OSS Gatekeeper usage, per-namespace configuration, and testability.

Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy referencing namespace ConfigMap values
- Per-tenant overrides via Namespace annotations/config
- Lightweight tests to verify enforcement
- Minimal YAML scaffolding for quick rollout checks

Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: defines RateLimitTemplate for K8sRateLimit
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sratelimittemplate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRateLimit
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sratelimit
      # Pseudocode: reads per-namespace cnf.rate-limit and enforces a per-minute cap
      defaultRate := 100
      rateLimitPerMin := data.rateLimitPerMin
      # implementation would map namespace to rate and count requests
      # returns deny if burst exceeds rate
```

```yaml
# Constraint: per-tenant rate limit value
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sRateLimit
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rate-limit
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      kinds: ["Namespace"]
  parameters:
    rateLimitPerMin: 200
    targetPath: "/gateway"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest overriding default rate for tenant-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    cnf.rate-limit: "200"  # override default 100/min
```

```yaml

kind: Pod
metadata:

spec:

    command: ["sh", "-c", "for i in {1..150}; do curl -s http://gateway-service/gateway || true; done"]
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical multi-tenant logging, ensuring tenant context is preserved, and validates end-to-end transport to a centralized sink.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant logging and enrichment
- Sidecar forwarder pattern
- Namespace-config driven behavior
- Secure transport to Loki

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-logs
  namespace: default
data:
  cnf.log.enabled: "true"
  cnf.log.target: "https://log-sink:3100/loki/api/v1/push"
  cnf.log.sample-rate: "0.5"
```
